title: GrapheneOS reveals what's finally making Motorola support possible
summary: GrapheneOS says Motorola support is on track for 2027, enabled by its partnership with Motorola Mobility and Qualcomm's security work plus Android 17's secure element-backed PIN/password rate limiting. Currently only Google Pixel devices meet the project's hardware security requirements; GrapheneOS layers extra protections such as longer passwords, optional fingerprint-plus-PIN second factor, hardened exploit mitigations, USB protections while locked, and configurable auto-reboot.

Jul 26, 2026 — 11:38 PM ET

Back at MWC 2026, Motorola and GrapheneOSannounced a long-term partnershipthat will end the latter’s long-standing exclusivity to Google Pixel phones. Now, GrapheneOS has reiterated that support for Motorola smartphones is on track for 2027.

WhileGrapheneOShas yet to say whether the partnership will produce a dedicated Motorola phone or simply extend support to existing or upcoming models, it has now highlighted the security advances, including Qualcomm’s contributions, that are paving the way for the expansion.

Ina lengthy post on X, the project noted that it currently only supports Google Pixel devices because they’re the only Android phones that meet its hardware security requirements. However, it added that this is expected to change in 2027, “thanks to our partnership with Motorola Mobility and progress being made by Qualcomm.”

The post also touched on Android’s evolving security features, highlightingthe secure element-backed PIN and password rate limitingthat’s now part ofAndroid 17.

Instead of allowing unlimited passcode attempts, Android 17 caps them at just 20 and progressively increases the delay after repeated failed attempts, increasing protection against brute-force attacks. GrapheneOS says it only supports devices that implement this latest generation of secure element protections.

The project also explained that Google’s Pixel phones have included secure element-based rate limiting and insider attack resistance since the Pixel 2, while GrapheneOS layers on additional protections such as longer password support, optional fingerprint plus second-factor PIN authentication, hardened exploit mitigations, USB protections while locked, and its own configurable auto-reboot feature.

For now, Pixel devices remain the only officially supported hardware for GrapheneOS. But with Qualcomm’s security roadmap continuing as planned, Motorola will become the first major Android manufacturer outside Google to officially support the privacy-focused operating system in 2027.

## Announcement and timeline

Back at MWC 2026, Motorola and GrapheneOS announced a long-term partnership that will end the latter’s long-standing exclusivity to Google Pixel phones. Now, GrapheneOS has reiterated that support for Motorola smartphones is on track for 2027.

While GrapheneOS has yet to say whether the partnership will produce a dedicated Motorola phone or simply extend support to existing or upcoming models, it has now highlighted the security advances, including Qualcomm’s contributions, that are paving the way for the expansion.

> “We currently only support Google Pixel devices because they’re the only Android phones that meet our hardware security requirements,” the project noted in a lengthy post on X.  
> “Thanks to our partnership with Motorola Mobility and progress being made by Qualcomm,” this is expected to change in 2027.

## Security advances

The post also touched on Android’s evolving security features, highlighting the secure element-backed PIN and password rate limiting that’s now part of Android 17.

Instead of allowing unlimited passcode attempts, Android 17 caps them at just 20 and progressively increases the delay after repeated failed attempts, increasing protection against brute-force attacks. GrapheneOS says it only supports devices that implement this latest generation of secure element protections.

> “Android 17 caps passcode attempts at just 20 and progressively increases the delay after repeated failed attempts,” the project explained.

## GrapheneOS protections

The project also explained that Google’s Pixel phones have included secure element-based rate limiting and insider attack resistance since the Pixel 2, while GrapheneOS layers on additional protections such as:

- Longer password support
- Optional fingerprint plus second-factor PIN authentication
- Hardened exploit mitigations
- USB protections while locked
- Its own configurable auto-reboot feature

## Current support and future plans

For now, Pixel devices remain the only officially supported hardware for GrapheneOS. But with Qualcomm’s security roadmap continuing as planned, Motorola will become the first major Android manufacturer outside Google to officially support the privacy-focused operating system in 2027.
